facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin lesions on her anterior thighs
lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier in recurrent 3‐day outbreaks
resolved spontaneously without residual injury
well‐defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology
central clearing, and purpuric edges
symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror‐image pattern
no systemic symptoms
no preceding infection
laboratory studies were within normal limits

complete blood count, biochemistry, urinalysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C‐reactive protein, complement levels (C3, C4, C1q), immunoglobulin levels, rheumatoid factor, and acute‐phase reactants were within normal limits
Antinuclear, anti–double‐stranded DNA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic, anti–Ro, anti–La, and transglutaminase antibodies were negative
Serologies for syphilis, hepatitis B and C viruses, HIV, cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, and parvovirus B19 were negative

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic targetoid appearance with central clearing and purpuric edges, which is consistent with erythema multiforme.
The patient's intensely pruritic skin lesions that resolve spontaneously without residual injury are consistent with urticaria.
The patient's skin lesions have an annular morphology and are symmetrically distributed, which is consistent with annular erythema.
The patient's skin lesions recur at the same locations and have a fixed pattern, which is consistent with fixed drug eruption.
The patient's intensely pruritic skin lesions that resolve spontaneously without residual injury could be consistent with an insect bite reaction.
The patient's skin lesions could be consistent with contact dermatitis, although there is no clear exposure history.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology and distribution, which could be consistent with pityriasis rosea.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology and are intensely pruritic, which could be consistent with nummular dermatitis.
The patient's intensely pruritic skin lesions could be consistent with atopic dermatitis, although there is no clear history of atopy.
The patient's skin lesions have a characteristic morphology and are accompanied by systemic symptoms, which could be consistent with Sweet syndrome, although the patient has no systemic symptoms.
